concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - extraction-layer, minted this batch on security-overview.json, not yet promoted to the registry

concepts.label: Couchbase Server user (administrator or application identity)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the generic Server-side identity that authenticates and is later authorized. No existing concept fits: sgw:user is a different product's Public-API identity, capella has no standalone 'user' concept (roles attach to org/project membership instead), and rbac-role:role/capella-role:role are role placeholders, not the user identity itself. Server's own generic user has never been minted.

concepts.label: Local authentication domain
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - per the batch's naming guidance for authentication domains. The local domain consists of users whose credentials Couchbase Server maintains itself.

concepts.label: External authentication domain
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of auth-domain:local. Consists of users whose credentials are maintained remotely.

concepts.label: Username/password authentication
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new namespace auth-mechanism:, for the concrete credential mechanisms this page names (as against auth-domain:, which is about where credentials are maintained, and idp:, which is about which external system does the maintaining).

concepts.label: X.509 certificate-based (mTLS) authentication
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of auth-mechanism:username-password. Distinct from privilege/role concepts entirely: this is how identity is established, before any RBAC check happens.

concepts.label: LDAP (external identity provider)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - per the batch's naming guidance: auth: already exists but both its members (auth:mfa, auth:sso) are Capella-labelled mechanisms, not this. New namespace idp: for external identity providers server/ actually integrates with.

concepts.label: SAML IdP (external identity provider)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sibling of idp:ldap. NOT merged with the promoted sso:realm/sso:group-mapping/sso:default-team family - those are explicitly Capella SSO concepts (Capella's own IdP-registration and team/group-mapping model) and this page states no relationship between the two; see cross_component_finding.

relations.subject: server:user
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - authenticatesVia ('which credential mechanism an access surface actually uses'). Stretched from access-surface-to-credential-type (its prior uses are all Capella data/management-plane surfaces) to user-to-domain; the shape - X is authenticated through mechanism/system Y - transfers cleanly even though the prior occurrences were all Capella. First positive data point that a Capella-minted predicate generalizes to Server without forcing.
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server assigns each user to one of two _authentication domains_: the _local_ domain consisting of users whose credentials are maintained by Couchbase Server itself; the _external_ domain consisting of users whose credentials are maintained remotely — for example, on an _LDAP_ server or a _SAML IdP_.

notable_absence.finding: Zero mentions of 'role', 'privilege', or 'RBAC' on this page. It is exclusively about establishing identity (authentication); the page's own second sentence explicitly defers authorization ('Subsequent to successful authentication, _authorization_ can be performed') to elsewhere. This is the cleanest possible confirmation that Server's docs treat authentication and authorization as two genuinely separate axes, matching the pre-existing registry note on auth:sso ('a genuinely separate axis from authorization') - except here that separation is stated of Server's own model, not just inferred by analogy from Capella's.

cross_component_finding: This page is the hub linking to four detail pages (authentication-overview, usernames-and-passwords, authentication-domains, certificates) that between them do most of the security/ subtree's authentication work - a much flatter, more explicit fan-out than security-overview.md's single-bullet treatment of the same topic. Content duplication watch: this page and authentication-overview.md open with the near-identical sentence ('To access Couchbase Server, users must be authenticated. _Authentication_ is a process for identifying who is attempting to access a system.') verbatim - the same three sentences appear as this page's second paragraph and as authentication-overview.md's page abstract. That is not paraphrase, it is copy-paste, and it recurs a third time as usernames-and-passwords.md's framing sentence in slightly reworded form ('Couchbase Server requires that administrators and applications _authenticate_...'). Three pages restate the same definitional paragraph rather than one page defining it and the others linking to it.
cross_product_finding: idp:ldap and idp:saml are minted fresh here rather than reusing the promoted sso:realm / sso:group-mapping / sso:default-team family, even though both are 'an external identity provider a user authenticates against' at the label level. Naming-collision discipline applied deliberately: Capella's SSO model registers an IdP under a 'realm' and maps IdP groups to Capella teams/roles via sso:group-mapping, a management-plane construct with no bucket/collection-scoped RBAC underneath it; Server's LDAP/SAML integration (detailed in authentication-domains.md) maps external identities into Server's own local/external domain and role/group system directly, with per-collection-scoped roles as the eventual destination. No page in either product states these are the same mechanism - they solve the same problem (federate to an external IdP) for two structurally different downstream authorization models, so they are kept as separate concepts per the batch's naming-collision rule rather than merged or cross-linked.
